messages:
yun: Heads-up — nightly translation eval spiked for CJK pairs (zh->ko, ja->zh). BLEU drop ~9-12 pts on nightly-translation-suite compared to yesterday. Failing prompts look like sampling truncation/hallucination patterns. Example from prompt T-7842:

yun: source: 我今天开会很晚，可能会晚到。
Baseline (gold): I have a late meeting today, may be late.
Model (nightly): I have a meeting today with the CEO and we will... <cuts off> then invents 'on the 3rd'

yun: Metrics snippet:
```
pair    BLEU_yesterday    BLEU_today
zh->ko  32.1              22.8
ja->zh  29.4              20.1
```

elena: ugh. did the quant or runtime flags change in the last deploy? :eyes:

jun: which job/run id? can you paste the nightly job link?

yun: nightly run <https://ci.redwood.ai/evals/translation/nightly/2026-03-18/17914|17914> - attached the failing prompt ids T-7842, T-7901, T-7920.

sara_ml: I pushed a compile tweak yesterday to try int8 dynamic for more models in the pool. flags: `--quantize=dynamic8 --kv-cache-quant=true`

mike_ops: kernel logs during the run show a few fallback messages: `WARN: fp16->int8 kernel fallback for attention_qk` and `WARN: inefficient GEMM path` — could degrade sampling behaviour.

elena: can we repro locally with the same seed and sampling config? maybe sampling params changed (temp/top_p)?

jun: checked config diffs — sampling params were stable. However `generation.max_tokens` was clipped from 128->64 in the nightly harness for speed; that could explain truncation but not the hallucinated additions.

sara_ml: note: we also changed `kv-cache-quant` to true which modifies cache storage layout; if cache corruption happens you can get weird token jumps.

jun: good call. plan:
1) reproduce one failing prompt with yesterday's build vs today's build (binary + compile flags)
2) run with/without `--quantize=dynamic8` and with larger `max_tokens`
3) collect raw logits + token ids for trace

ai-evals-bot: nightly job 17914 flagged regression threshold breach for zh->ko, ja->zh. See full diff: <https://ci.redwood.ai/evals/diffs/17914|diff-17914>

mike_ops: quick repro command (local):
```bash
python reproduce.py --model /models/nightly/17914 --prompt-id T-7842 --seed 42 --temp 0.8 --top-p 0.9 --max-tokens 128 --dump-tokens dump.json
```

elena: i'll run that now on a small GPU node. tagging @jun and @sara_ml to collect flags.

elena: quick update — with `--quantize=dynamic8` enabled we do see divergence in logits after step ~27, token IDs diverge, and the generated continuation is different from baseline. Without `--quantize=dynamic8` the output matches baseline.

jun: that isolates it to the dynamic8 path. can you capture raw kv cache binary? maybe quantization lib bug.

yun: archival note — failing examples saved to /artifacts/evals/17914/cjk_regressions.tar.gz

sara_ml: reassigning to infra-quant team — filing issue: QNT-462: dynamic8 kv-cache mismatch on CJK multi-token sequences. attaching reproducer and dumps.

mike_ops: temporary mitigation: revert `--quantize=dynamic8` in nightly pipeline (I can patch the job). should we do that now?

jun: yes patch nightly to revert and re-run, mark as hotfix. we'll continue root-cause on QNT-462.

elena: patched pipeline and kicked off new nightly run: <https://ci.redwood.ai/evals/translation/nightly/17915|17915> — will monitor.

yun: thanks all. next steps: infra-quant to bisect quant lib changes, eng-runtime to add kv-cache CRC check in debug builds, and evals to add a focused CJK prompt subset to catch this early. assigning owners: QNT-462 -> @sara_ml, RUNTIME-201 -> @jun, EVALS-789 -> @yun. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Created issue QNT-462 and linked job artifacts.

elena: re-run results look restored (BLEU diff back within noise). closing nightly alert for now. :relieved:
